turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Step 1 — What separates high from low fatigue strength?**

The dataset splits into clear process families:

| Process regime | Target range |
|---|---|
| Normalized only (THT=30, TT=30) | 225–275 |
| Through-hardened + tempered (THT≈825–865, TT=420–680) | 325–906 |
| **Carburized (NT=930, CT=930, DT≈850–896, TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5)** | **838–1190** |

The carburizing route dominates. All samples above 1000 MPa share: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, DT=850–895.8, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, TT=160–200, low carbon (C≈0.17–0.23).

**Step 2 — Within the carburized group, what drives the top?**

Best rows (1124, 1190 MPa): Ni≈1.69, Cr≈0.55, Mo≈0.18, C≈0.23, Si≈0.35, Mn≈0.51, very low P (0.008), low S. The Cr-heavy variant (Cr≈1.17, Ni low) also reaches 1074–1144. The Ni–Cr–Mo case-hardening chemistry (like SNCM-type steel) is the most consistent, remaining >1050 across Ct (140–540), QmT (60–140), DT (850–896), Dt (15–70) — an intrinsically **broad** optimum.

**Step 3 — Robustness choices (±5% single-variable perturbations)**

- **Ct**: high results exist at 130, 340, 470, 540 → pick mid-high 500 (flat region).
- **DT/Dt**: both (850, 15) and (895.8, 70.2) give >1100 → pick interior point (870, 40).
- **QmT**: 60 and 140 both give >1100 → pick 100 (middle of a flat plateau).
- **TT**: 160 and 200 both excellent → pick 180.
- **NT=930, CT=930**: −5% = 883.5, still in austenitizing/carburizing regime — targets don't collapse.
- **Chemistry**: Ni=1.7, Cr=0.6, Mo=0.18, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.60 — ±5% keeps us inside the cluster of 1030–1190 MPa samples.
- **Impurities/defects**: minimize P, S, dA, dB, dC (but keep P/S at low observed levels 0.008/0.012 rather than absolute extremes, since ±5% there is trivial).
- **RedRatio**: 690–860 all appear in top rows → pick 800.

This recipe sits in the center of the highest-performing, flattest region of the data rather than on a single record's sharp peak.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=500, DT=870, Dt=40, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.60, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.7, Cr=0.6, Cu=0.08, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=800, dA=0.02, dB=0.0, dC=0.0**
